_what: Declarative watch list for the VAST ternary watchdog (.github/workflows/ternary-vast-watchdog.yml).
_why: The GCP watchdog (ternary-leg-watchdog.yml) cannot watch a Vast leg: it authenticates by WIF, reads state from GCS, asks 'is a gcp-ternary VM up?', and its only recovery is to re-dispatch the GCP workflow. Pointing a Vast leg at it would produce monitoring that silently watches nothing. Under the 2026-07-25 all-runs-on-Vast directive that gap would apply to every GPU run the program makes from here.
_how: The workflow runs on a cron. Per enabled entry it asks three questions against S3 and the Vast API: is leg.json already there (DONE), is an instance up AND the committed iteration count HIGHER than last tick (RUNNING), or is it dead/stalled? Only a DIED entry relaunches, resuming from the last committed checkpoint; a stall is an alert, because a relaunch would hang the same way. A per-UTC-day relaunch counter in S3 caps runaway re-dispatch and every outcome is an annotation; any alert also FAILS the job so GitHub's own failure notification fires.
_alive_is_not_advancing: The Vast-specific correction over the GCP version. A rented instance can sit up with a dead container or an idle GPU and look perfectly healthy, so RUNNING requires the commit store to have ADVANCED, not merely for an instance to exist.
_capacity_refusal: A start answered with {'success': false, 'error': 'resources_unavailable'} is NOT a preemption and is NOT waited out: destroy, add the machine to the exclusion set, pick another host. That policy lives in ternary_vast_launch.collect + ResourceSpec.exclude_machine_ids and is delegated to, never duplicated.
_editing: Set enabled=false when a unit is finished or deliberately parked — do NOT delete the entry, so the history of what was watched stays legible. The watchdog is a no-op on an empty or all-disabled list.
_required_keys_are_enforced: Every parameter that KEYS THE COMMIT PREFIX or the code the host runs must appear on each enabled entry, because the watchdog relaunches from these values alone. The prefix is <leg_id>_r<seed>[_dir<direction>]_dt<timestep_fs>fs_wu<warmup_timestep_fs>_<mode>, so an entry missing one would make the watchdog 'resume' a DIFFERENT trajectory than the run it is watching. git_branch is required for the same reason and is easy to miss: a schedule only fires from the default branch, so github.ref_name inside the watchdog is 'main' — without recording the branch a unit was launched from, a relaunch would pull main's code onto a feature branch's checkpoint. Validated by watchdog_validate.py on every pass; an incomplete entry aborts the pass rather than relaunching the wrong thing.
